2609.31505.title: Prompt Minimization: Reducing Input Redundancy Without Sacrificing Output Fidelity
2609.31505.paper_summary: Despite the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs), prompt design remains largely heuristic and ad hoc. This project will explore $\textit{prompt minimization}$, the process of reducing prompts to their smallest, most information-dense form while preserving output fidelity. Practically, shorter prompts reduce computational overhead and inference latency, especially when large contexts, such as entire documents or codebases, are included unnecessarily. Further, longer prompts can damage LLM reasoning and accuracy. Theoretically, the existence of multiple prompts yielding equivalent outputs suggests a high degree of redundancy in the input space, raising fundamental questions about what information is essential to elicit specific model behaviors. We propose three variant frameworks to identify and evaluate minimal prompts and demonstrate that minimal prompts often produce outputs comparable to those of their longer counterparts. These findings suggest new directions for efficient prompt engineering and deepen our understanding of input compression in LLMs.
2609.31505.paper_summary_zh: 儘管大型語言模型（LLMs）的能力不斷增強，但提示設計仍然主要是啟發式和臨時的。這個項目將探討 $\textit{提示最小化}$，即在保持輸出忠實度的同時，將提示縮減到最小、信息密度最高的形式。實際上，較短的提示可以減少計算開銷和推理延遲，特別是在包含不必要的大上下文時，例如整個文檔或代碼庫。此外，較長的提示可能會損害 LLM 的推理和準確性。理論上，存在多個提示產生等效輸出的情況表明輸入空間中存在高度的冗餘，這引發了關於什麼信息對於引發特定模型行為是必需的基本問題。我們提出三種變體框架來識別和評估最小提示，並展示最小提示通常能產生與其較長對應物相當的輸出。這些發現為高效的提示工程指明了新的方向，並加深了我們對 LLM 中輸入壓縮的理解。
